newsitem.title: USA: Floodwaters swamp parts of Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Floodwaters swamp parts of Illinois.

text.p: The Rock River broke through a railroad embankment Tuesday, sending muddy floodwaters across Illinois farm fields in an area where two small towns have been cut off, police said.
The Whiteside County sheriff's office told area residents to prepare to move to higher ground, even as forecasters warned that more heavy rain could hit the region later in the week.

The railroad embankment southwest of Erie, Illinois, gave way at dawn, the sheriff's office said, sending water across a road and further isolating the town of 1,500 about 130 miles (210 km) west of Chicago.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers said the water was coming through the embankment in four or five places, threatening homes on the west side of Erie. Police were going door to door to warn residents of the danger.

Erie and a neighboring town on the river, Hillsdale, have been the hardest hit by the high water triggered by a freak four-inch (10.1 cm) rainfall last week. A levee that broke last weekend and rising waters have flooded about 15,000 acres in the region.
Hillsdale, a small crossroads village, has been evacuated, the Illinois Emergency Management Agency said.

In the north-central part of the state the Illinois River at Peoria was rising more slowly than had earlier been forecast and no major problems were reported. A parking lot on the city's downtown riverfront was under water but a popular restaurant at its edge remained open for business, protected by sandbags.
Cottages and homes along the river to the north of Peoria were cut off, with some residents traveling back and forth by boat to check on their possessions.
State officials said no major roads were closed by high water and there had been no deaths blamed on the flooding.
Forecasters at Weather Services Corp. warned that a storm developing in Texas appeared headed on the same path as the one that triggered the current flooding.
They said as much as two inches of rain could fall over northern and central Illinois, beginning as early as Wednesday night.
The full impact of the current high water was still to come along the Illinois River in many areas downstream from Peoria.
